webhook.title: Create an inbound webhook
webhook.intro: b24 copies a Bitrix24 portal's CRM: deals, leads, contacts and companies. It reads them through an inbound webhook and changes them only with your permission. The webhook acts with the rights of the employee who creates it.
webhook.steps:
In Bitrix24:

1. Open **Developer resources**.
2. Go to **Common use cases** → **Other** → **Inbound webhook**.
3. Under **Assign permissions**, tick the permissions below.
4. Click **Create**. Bitrix24 shows the webhook's address.
scopes.title: Permissions to tick
scope.crm: **CRM** (`{code}`): required. Deals, leads, contacts, companies, products and activities.
scope.user_basic: **Users (basic)** (`{code}`): required. b24 checks who made the webhook, and reads employees' names and e-mails. **Users** (`user`) works too.
scope.department: **Company Structure** (`{code}`): recommended. Departments and their heads, so the copy knows who reports to whom.
scope.task: **Tasks** (`{code}`): optional. The Bitrix24 tasks on your deals and leads.
scope.telephony: **Telephony** (`{code}`): optional, for calls. The portal's call history. The employee also needs the right to view call statistics.
scope.disk: **Drive** (`{code}`): optional, for files: client documents, the files of deals and their attachments. Useful once b24 can work with files.
scope.documentgenerator: **Document Generator** (`{code}`): optional, for documents made from templates. Bitrix24's docs place the CRM's document methods under `crm` on one page and under this scope on another, so tick both.
webhook.access: No **Inbound webhook** item? An administrator allows it in **Settings** → **Bitrix24 settings** → **Security** → **Bitrix24 integrations**, in the field **Who can create inbound webhooks**.
address.title: Paste the webhook's address
address.where: Copy the address Bitrix24 shows for the webhook and paste it here.
address.label: Webhook address
address.hint: Kept in your system keyring or, without one, in a file only you can read.
address.secret: The address works like a password: anyone who has it can do what the webhook's employee can. Do not send it to anyone.
check.title: Checking the webhook
check.body: b24 asks the portal who made the webhook. It saves the address only if the portal answers.
failed.title: The check did not pass
failed.body: The webhook or the portal did not pass b24's check, so nothing was saved. Check the address and your connection, then try again.
done.title: Connected
done.body: The profile is ready. Copy the portal's CRM into WireCat, then list the open deals:
done.app.title: Advanced: a local application instead
done.app:
A webhook acts as the employee who made it. A local application acts as the employee who signs in. An administrator creates it once:

1. **Developer resources** → **Common use cases** → **Other** → **Local application**.
2. Choose **Server**. Set **Your handler path** to `https://wirecat.dev/webhooks/apps/b24-callback`. Leave **Initial installation path** and **Menu item text** empty, and **Application completes the installation itself** off.
3. Under **Assign permissions**, tick the same permissions, then save.
4. Copy the **Application ID (client_id)** and the **Application key (client_secret)**.
